question: Given a fixed sensing budget, how much does differentiably optimized placement matter compared with simply adding probes?

naive_family.description: Conventional vertically aligned wake probes at x = 1, the family used by the committed identifiability study.
naive_family.ns8_note: The committed family uses a 0.4 pitch centred on zero. That rule cannot reach 8 probes inside y in [-1, 1], so Ns=8 is defined as 8 evenly spaced probes spanning [-0.9, 0.9]. This is deliberately generous to the naive baseline: it gives it more coverage than the Ns=5 span, so the comparison does not understate what naive probes achieve.

optimized_family.method: T3 WakeSurrogate -> T4 SensorArrayDesign, reverse-mode gradient (T4 VJP -> T3 VJP), L-BFGS-B with box bounds. No CFD enters the design loop.

tau_protocol.optimization: per sensor count, solved so the soft-minimum weight perplexity N_eff = 10 at that count's NAIVE layout, then frozen for that count's campaign
tau_protocol.cross_count_comparison: D_tau depends on tau, so values calibrated per count are NOT comparable across counts. Cross-count claims use (a) the hard minimum retained pair distance, which is tau-free, and (b) D_tau at a single common tau calibrated at the Ns=2 naive layout.

primary_metric.name: hard minimum retained pair distance on real CFD
primary_metric.definition: min over retained pairs of ||m_i - m_j||^2 / (Ns*5*2)
primary_metric.why: Normalised per scalar measurement, so it is directly comparable across sensor counts, and tau-free.

evaluation.source: existing 66-angle real-CFD bank (T1 -> T2), no new CFD

prespecified_headline_test: Does Ns=2 optimized match or exceed Ns=5 naive on the real-CFD hard minimum? Recorded as a prediction before the optimization was run.
terminology: Reported as global discrimination / measurement discrimination. No information-theoretic claim is made.
out_of_scope: physical (CFD-in-the-loop) refinement of the ablation designs
